title: What If a Lake Lost 90 Percent of Its Water? Lake Chad Did

scenes.text: What if a lake shrank to a tenth of its size? Lake Chad did.
In 1963, Lake Chad covered about 25,000 square kilometers.
By 2001 it was under 1,500, a loss of roughly nine tenths of its surface.
Fish production fell by about 60 percent, and grazing land degraded, leaving less feed for livestock.
Cameroon, Chad, Niger and Nigeria now compete for the water, which the UN warned could drive migration and conflict.
Nearly 30 million people live along its shores, around a lake that lost almost nine tenths of its surface.
